newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - unchanged to up 1/8.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - unchanged to up 1/8.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were unchanged to up 1/8 point in light trading on Tuesday as the primary market received its new offerings.
"New issue pricing was firm to strong in the negotiated and competitive sectors," a municipal bond analyst said.
Overall, dollar bonds were up 1/8 and high grade bonds were basically unchanged on the day.
The secondary market was light, with an assortment of bid lists circulating - none of any real size, traders said.
In primary action, BancAmerica Securities won the largest new issue Tuesday, a $525 million California general obligation bond deal. The firm reoffered the 2026 maturity at a 5.80 percent yield.
In the negotiated sector, two Pennsylvania housing issues were priced and repriced by their respective syndicates.
Merrill Lynch & Co repriced a $50 million Pennsylvania Housing Finance Agency single-family mortgage revenue bond issue, series 1997-56A (AMT).
PaineWebber Inc repriced a $50 million Pennsylvania Housing Finance Agency single-family mortgage revenue bond issue, series 1997-57A (AMT) and 1997-57B (NON-AMT).
Looking ahead to Wednesday, traders expect a weak consumer price index when it is released at 0830 EST.
Municipal bond sales for Wednesday are expected to total $1.4 billion in 32 sales.
Negotiated offerings total $1.2 billion in 22 sales, with a $316 million Palm Beach County deal through Smith Barney Inc. topping the the list.
On the competitive side, 10 sales totaling $289 million are on the schedule, a $226 million Louisiana deal at 1100 EST is the largest.
An additional five sales totaling $62 million are on the possible calender, meaning underwriters have said they may price the bonds Wednesday, depending on market conditions.
